learning_outcomes.text: Have systematic knowledge and understanding of the key concepts and aspects for the calculation and design of lightweight structures.

Have adequate knowledge of the calculation and design of lightweight structures, including cutting-edge knowledge in this field of mechanical engineering, such as the design and calculation of composite material structures.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve lightweight structure problems using established methods.
Be able to choose and apply analytical and modeling methods to solve lightweight structure problems.
Understand the different calculation methods used for the analysis of lightweight structures.
Be able to combine theory and practice to solve lightweight structure problems.
Understand the different applicable methods and techniques and their limitations for the design and calculation of lightweight structures.
Be aware of the implications of engineering practice in the design and calculation of lightweight structures.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
Adequate knowledge of their engineering branch, including some cutting-edge knowledge in their field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and carry out experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
Understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.
Awareness of all the implications of engineering practice.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility, and standards of engineering practice.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences usually demonstrated by developing and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering to meet the required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Bending of thin-walled section beams
Topic 2. Uniform torsion of thin-walled tubular profiles
Topic 3. Introduction to the theory of composite material beams and sandwich beams
assessment_rules: Continuous assessment makes up 100% of the grade, structured as: 30% for laboratory practices, 40% for continuous assessment tests 1, and 30% for continuous assessment tests 2. Attendance and completion of scheduled laboratory practices are mandatory to pass the course. The use of AI tools is selectively permitted; instructors will specify guidelines for their use and how students must describe their application. Academic fraud involving AI tools will be subject to the University Carlos III de Madrid's regulations.
